deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a working draft of Riemann's analysis of when the theta function theta(u - e) vanishes identically on the surface. That analysis appears in print as 'Ueber das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen' (Crelle 65, 1865/66). The previous page is a degree count (w - 2n = 2p - 2) for branch points and poles. Notation, as in Riemann: (s,z) or (epsilon,zeta) is a point of the p-gonal surface. alpha_pi^(nu) or u_pi^(nu) is the value of the normalized first-kind integral u_pi at the point (eta_nu, zeta_nu). Congruence (==) is modulo the period lattice. Riemann's constant is absorbed into the normalization, so the zero set reads cleanly.

(A) Top paragraph (heavily corrected). Riemann has the theorem that theta(u_1 - sum_1^{p-1} alpha_1^(nu), ..., u_p - sum_1^{p-1} alpha_p^(nu)) vanishes identically in (s,z) for arbitrary p-1 points. From this he infers the following. If sum m < p, the argument (u - sum_1^{p-m} alpha^(nu) - b) can, for arbitrary positions of the variable points and of the p-m points eta, be brought to the form (-sum alpha^(nu)) (one fewer point, as needed). The device is to let one of the points epsilon coincide with (s,z), so that its integral cancels u. Hence theta(u - sum_1^{p-m} alpha - b) = 0 for every value system of these point pairs. In modern terms: a theta value whose argument is the Abel image of an effective divisor of degree p-1 (up to the Riemann constant) is zero.

(B) Jacobi inversion. Consider the congruence (e_1, ..., e_p) == (sum_1^p alpha_1^(nu), ..., sum_1^p alpha_p^(nu)) for given e.
- If theta(u - e) is not identically zero as a function of (s,z), it has exactly p zeros eta_1, ..., eta_p. These solve the congruence, and the solution is unique ("nur eine Lösung").
- If theta(u - e) vanishes for every (s,z), then (u^(nu) - e) == -sum_1^{p-1} alpha for every point, by (A) read in reverse. Hence e == sum_1^p alpha holds with one point free, so there are infinitely many solutions. Differentiating gives sum_{nu=1}^p d alpha_pi^(nu) = 0 for pi = 1, ..., p. That is, the p points can move continuously while the Abel sum stays fixed.

(C) Characterizing the indeterminate case. The p point pairs (epsilon_pi, zeta_pi) are then such that some quantity xi (a differential / linear combination of the du) becomes infinitely small of the second order. They can vary so that the remaining p-2 roots of xi = 0 stay constant. Modern reading: the p points, together with p-2 further points, form the 2p-2 zeros of an abelian differential of the first kind.
- Label the integrals at those p-2 further points u^(p+1), ..., u^(2p-2).
- Then (sum_1^{2p-2} u^(nu)) == 0, because the zeros of a holomorphic differential have Abel image 0 in Riemann's normalization.
- Therefore e == -(sum_{p+1}^{2p-2} u^(nu)).
- And theta(u - e) = theta(u + sum_{p+1}^{2p-2} u^(nu), ...), which vanishes identically by (A).

(D) Conclusion. A given system (e_1, ..., e_p) can be brought to the form (sum_1^p alpha^(nu)) in only one way if it is not congruent to a system of the form (-sum_1^{p-2} alpha^(nu)). It can be done in infinitely many ways if it is.

(E) Final lines (crossed out and restarted). Terminology: 2p-2 points with sum_1^{2p-2} alpha^(nu) == 0 are to be called 'verschwindende Punkte' (points of vanishing). Given p-1 arbitrary points, the remaining p-1 are then determined.
errors: No mathematical error is visible in the logic. Several statements are elliptical drafts, e.g. 'unendlich klein von der zweiten Ordnung' without saying of which function.
In (A) the upper summation limit fluctuates between p-m and p-1. In the formula theta(sum_p^{2p-2} u^(nu)) the lower limit should be p+1, consistent with the line above; this is a slip.

The implication 'theta(u - e) vanishes identically ⇒ (u - e) == -sum_1^{p-1}' is used without proof here. It relies on the earlier theorem that the zeros of theta(u - e) are characterized in this way.

results.what: theta(u - sum of p-1 Abel images) vanishes identically, i.e. the theta divisor is W_{p-1} up to the Riemann constant.
results.modern_name: Riemann vanishing theorem (theta divisor = W_{g-1} + kappa)

results.what: The Jacobi inversion e == sum_1^p alpha has a unique solution unless e == -(sum of p-2 points). In that case there are infinitely many solutions, and the p points together with p-2 others are the zeros of a holomorphic differential.
results.modern_name: Uniqueness of Jacobi inversion / special divisors of degree g (l(D) > 1 iff D is special, Riemann-Roch)

results.what: The Abel image of the zeros of an abelian differential is congruent to 0 (sum over 2p-2 points), with constants normalized.
results.modern_name: Abel image of the canonical divisor = -2 kappa (Riemann constant)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material Riemann published in 'Ueber das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen' (1865). The content is known and credited to him; the page only shows the working form of the argument.

checkable.asserts: For p=1 the theta divisor is the single point kappa = 1/2 + tau/2, matching W_{p-1} = W_0 shifted by the Riemann constant (result approx 0).
